newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Judge reviews U.S. jurisdiction in Holocaust suits.
newsitem.headline: Judge reviews U.S. jurisdiction in Holocaust suits.

text.p: Swiss banks said on Friday that a federal judge in New York was reviewing whether U.S. courts can hear lawsuits charging them with hoarding billions of dollars in unclaimed deposits of Holocaust victims.

The banks said Judge Edward Korman of the Eastern District of New York had agreed on Thursday to rule whether U.S. courts had any jurisdiction to consider three class-action lawsuits seeking billions of dollars in damages.

In the suits filed since October, claimants including Holocaust survivors and heirs are demanding money or bank records from Swiss banks including the three biggest -- Credit Suisse Group, Union Bank of Switzerland and Swiss Bank Corp.
SBC and Credit Suisse said the judge had agreed to a defence request to examine whether U.S. courts could hear the cases, which the banks dispute.
"The positive aspect for us is that he will now examine the question of jurisdiction," Credit Suisse spokesman Christoph Meier said. "This is certainly satisfactory for us."

Swiss banks have faced sharp criticism for their conduct during World War Two. Jewish groups say the banks may be holding billions of dollars in wealth left by the victims of Nazi mass-murder and have stonewalled relatives trying to track it down.
But the banks say the claims of individuals in the lawsuits can better be settled out of court.

The banks argue that they and the Swiss government have taken a range of steps to address the allegations, including creating an independent panel to search for unclaimed wealth that may have escaped two previous audits.
Banks, Swiss businesses and the Swiss central bank have also pledged more than 265 million Swiss francs ($180 million) to a memorial fund that will support needy Holocaust victims.

The government has established a commission of historians to probe neutral Switzerland's wartime role as a financial centre. It has also proposed selling part of its official gold reserves to finance a huge humanitarian fund.
Class-action suits are filed by plaintiffs in the belief they represent an entire class of potential claimants whose suits can be combined into one. ($ = 1.47 Swiss Francs)
